Alice Moreau [16/Sep 9:43am -07] wrote:
> Right, so a package that has been maintained by four people over
> eleven years ends up with a list of years that nobody can check
> against anything, and the only honest answer is the range that the
> version control history gives us. Every other answer I have seen
> proposed in this thread either asks the maintainer to remember what
> happened before they took the package over, or asks the reader to
> trust a number that nobody has checked since the year it was typed.

I agree that the history is the better record, but it is not the record
the licence asks for, and the two of them disagree in exactly the cases
where somebody is likely to look: a file imported from another project,
a patch applied on behalf of somebody who never had commit access, and
the year a package sat unchanged while its maintainer was away. What I
would rather have is a tool that writes the range from the history and
says so in a comment, so that the next person knows where the numbers
came from and can disagree with them in one place.

--
Bob Nowak

On Tue, Sep 16, 2026 at 09:12AM, Carol Iyer wrote:
> The description in the binding says the controller is optional, which
> contradicts the example two paragraphs further down, where it is
> required for every board that has the second power rail.

That contradiction is mine, and it comes from the board I had on my desk
when I wrote the first draft, which is the only one in the family that
can run without the rail. The others cannot, and the example is right
about them. I will make the description say that the controller is
required unless the second rail is absent, which is the shape the other
bindings in this directory use, and which at least has the virtue of
being checkable by a program rather than by a reader.

--- a/doc/bindings/example-controller.txt
+++ b/doc/bindings/example-controller.txt
@@ -12,7 +12,9 @@ Required properties:
-  - control-gpios: optional, see the example below
+  - control-gpios: required unless the second supply is absent; the
+    example below shows the only board in the family that omits it

 Optional properties:
   - label: a human readable name for the controller
